create.name: Western Chan Fellowship
create.bio:
The Western Chan Fellowship is a lay Buddhist association in the UK that practises Chan, the Chinese form of Zen. It grew out of local groups that formed after Chan Master Sheng Yen first taught in Britain in 1989; John Crook founded it in 1997 as its first teacher with Sheng Yen as its patron, and it is now a registered charity. Since 2011 its guiding teacher has been Simon Child, one of Sheng Yen's Dharma heirs, and his own heirs Fiona Nuttall and Rebecca Li also teach for it.

Its main work is silent residential retreats, held at present at Shawbottom Farm in the Peak District: week-long Silent Illumination and koan retreats, and the Western Zen Retreat, which joins sitting with an intensive, guided process of self-inquiry. Fees come with a half-price supported rate. A network of local sitting groups meets across England and Wales and in Warsaw, and the website keeps a large free library of articles, recorded talks and liturgy, along with its journal New Chan Forum.

courses.title: Western Zen Retreat (5 nights, Shawbottom Farm)
courses.description: A five-night residential retreat led by Simon Child in the Peak District. Silent sitting is combined with an intensive process of self-inquiry, supported by regular interviews with the teachers.

courses.title: Zen Koan Retreat (7 nights, Shawbottom Farm)
courses.description: A seven-night silent retreat led by Simon Child for working with a koan or hua-tou as the central practice. Individual interviews support the practice through the week.

courses.title: Silent Illumination Zen Retreat (7 nights, Shawbottom Farm)
courses.description: A seven-night silent retreat led by Fiona Nuttall in the Chan method of Silent Illumination, with instruction and private interviews. Suitable for deepening an established sitting practice.

free_resources.title: Audio and video talks
free_resources.description: The fellowship's archive of recorded Dharma talks and conference sessions, including talks by John Crook on koan practice and papers from its gatherings on engaged Buddhism, free to stream or download.

free_resources.title: Articles for newcomers to Chan
free_resources.description: A short selection of starter articles from the fellowship's library, including an introduction to Chan practice, picked to help new readers find their way into a large archive.
